title: Race, Outsider and Venice
welcome_lead: Othello's Moorishness is central. Examine race in early modern Venice and modern critical readings.
meta_desc: Race, the outsider and Venetian context in Othello at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have read race in Othello — early modern construction and modern critical reframing both essential.

concepts.def: Poetics: tragic hero's error or flaw causes downfall; Othello's jealousy, Macbeth's ambition, Lear's pride.
Purgation of pity and fear in audience; tragedy's moral function; debated by AC Bradley (1904).
Moor of Venice manipulated by Iago into killing Desdemona; race, jealousy, manipulation; tragic Othello restores honour.
Aged king divides kingdom by daughters' flattery; Cordelia banished, Goneril and Regan turn; tragic recognition of madness.
Shakespearean Tragedy; character-based criticism; tragic hero exceptional but flawed; lasting influence.

concepts.term: G. Wilson Knight Wheel of Fire 1930
concepts.def: Spatial pattern criticism; opposes Bradley's character focus; reads symbolic structures and imagery.

walkthroughs.body_html: The play's first scene establishes Othello entirely through racial slurs before he appears. The audience hears Iago and Roderigo's prejudiced framing before Othello's own measured eloquence corrects it.
Cyprus is Venice's military frontier. Once isolated there, Othello loses the civic constraints of Venice. The play's tragic mechanics depend on this geographical move.

Post-colonial and race-conscious critics read Othello's collapse as also a collapse into the racist script others have prepared for him.

His final speech ('one that loved not wisely but too well') is read with renewed attention to its self-othering.
